content: Fidaxomicin is a macrolide antibiotic specifically used to treat severe intestinal infections caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile)-associated diarrhea. This condition may occur rarely after the use of antibiotics and is characterized by persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain or cramping, and the presence of blood or mucus in the stool. Fidaxomicin works locally in the intestines and is minimally absorbed into the bloodstream, making it effective only for this type of bacterial infection. It is not suitable for treating other infections, including viral illnesses such as the common cold or flu. Usage Instructions: Before starting fidaxomicin, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, typically twice daily (every 12 hours). If using the liquid form, remove the bottle from the refrigerator 15 minutes before use and shake it well before measuring the dose with a proper measuring device or spoon. To achieve the best results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. While rare, serious allergic reactions can occur, including symptoms such as difficulty breathing, rash, itching, or swelling (especially of the face, throat, or tongue). If you experience any severe reactions, discontinue the medication and seek immediate medical attention. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Precautions: Before taking fidaxomicin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin), or any inactive ingredients in the product. This medication may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, fidaxomicin should only be used if clearly needed, as there is limited data on its safety. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding mothers should weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against the potential risks to the infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of fidaxomicin or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your doctor or pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergency situations, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S.). Storage: Store fidaxomicin tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. For the liquid form, keep it refrigerated in its original bottle and discard any unused medication after 12 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into drains unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of expired or unused medication. Important Notes: This summary does not contain all possible information about fidaxomicin. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
